findings.body: If Claude asks a question while leaving uncommitted changes, a successful commit nudge replaces that answer with its own text. `_question` then records no question, allowing work and close to proceed without an answer. The design route has the same overwrite at worker.py:185. Conversely, Codex ignores a successful nudge's answer at worker.py:208–210, so a question first asked there is lost. Preserve pending questions across nudges and inspect both providers' nudge answers.
findings.title: Not done: worker questions on both worker paths

findings.body: The turn-log count includes Codex's commit-nudge turn, although that turn finishes the same worker round. After a first round containing two turns, the next invocation computes round 3; this `max` preserves that value instead of advancing the persisted round from 1 to 2. The worker, test, review and CI timings consequently carry the wrong round. Use the persisted worker-round counter once available, and cover consecutive rounds containing a nudge.
findings.title: Not done: the item's round number on every timing record

findings.body: Sign-off reviews never reach this writer: the sign-off branch returns at review.py:508 or refuses at lines 493–507. Its real caller, records.py:286, invokes `review.signoff` directly, so close's failure-result recorder cannot cover it either. Clean, blocking and failed sign-off reviews therefore produce run events but no review-result occurrence with a fresh id. Record results for this supported review path as well.
findings.title: Not done: every review result has a fresh id

findings.body: The new producer tests use freshly configured repositories already pinned to the current release. None exercises these records after upgrading a client adopted on the previous release, as the repository's review rule explicitly requires. The existing previous-release scenario at tests/test_upgrade_command.py:477 checks upgrade output and synced files, but asserts none of the new timing, occurrence or question behavior. Add that client-upgrade case to the command-boundary producer coverage.
findings.title: Not done: run-record coverage for previously adopted client repos

findings.body: Both cache-hit returns at review.py:296 and :302 return `SKIPPED`, whose text also starts with a backtick. This classifier therefore records them as `passed`. For example, retrying close after tests passed but the review failed appends a near-zero passed test timing despite executing no tests. Distinguish execution from cache reuse explicitly so cached stages receive the skipped outcome.
findings.title: Classify cached test stages as skipped
